assurance_boundary.statement: OpenPost does not claim SOC 2 or ISO 27001 certification, an independent security audit, or an independent penetration-test report. No current certification, audit report, or penetration-test report is published for reliance.

incident_history.statement: OpenPost currently has no incident entries in this public register. This means no incident has been disclosed here; it is not a guarantee that no security or privacy event has ever occurred.
incident_history.publication_commitment: When the operator confirms a material managed-service incident, OpenPost will add the date, affected service and data, customer action, and remediation status when disclosure is lawful and does not increase risk.

control_matrix.control: Identity, sessions, roles, and workspace access
control_matrix.application: Hashes passwords, supports TOTP and passkeys, records revocable browser sessions, and enforces organization, workspace, scope, and action checks.
control_matrix.managed_service: Configures hosted identity options, preserves the break-glass administrator boundary, and responds to verified account or access incidents.
control_matrix.self_hosted_operator: Chooses identity providers and administrator accounts, protects recovery access, reviews members and sessions, and removes access promptly.
control_matrix.customer_or_provider: Users protect their sign-in methods and devices. A selected identity provider controls its own authentication and account-recovery process.

control_matrix.application: Encrypts stored social tokens, TOTP secrets, OIDC client secrets, and saved provider-app secrets with AES-256-GCM; API-family bearer tokens are stored as hashes.
control_matrix.managed_service: Supplies and protects the encryption key and hosted provider credentials outside the image and repository and limits production access to the disclosed operator boundary.
control_matrix.self_hosted_operator: Generates, stores, rotates, backs up, and restricts the encryption key, JWT secret, social app credentials, and email or storage credentials.
control_matrix.customer_or_provider: Users revoke connections or access tokens they no longer need. Social and identity providers protect and can revoke their provider-side credentials.

control_matrix.control: TLS, host, database, media, and network boundary
control_matrix.application: Uses secure cookie attributes on HTTPS, validates trusted origins and redirect targets, and accesses database and media through configured service boundaries.
control_matrix.managed_service: Terminates public TLS, keeps direct host and database access inside the disclosed operator boundary, and configures the current managed data locations and providers.
control_matrix.self_hosted_operator: Places OpenPost behind correctly configured TLS, restricts database and media access, patches the host and reverse proxy, and chooses where data is stored.
control_matrix.customer_or_provider: Hosting, network, storage, and social providers secure the infrastructure and endpoints they control under their own terms.

control_matrix.application: Enforces authenticated role and workspace checks. Submitting a support request does not change the user's application authorization.
control_matrix.managed_service: Uses the named key-only operator and sudo boundary described in the trust register. Routine application work is automated; exceptional access is limited to the stated support, recovery, security, abuse, legal, or fraud purpose.
control_matrix.self_hosted_operator: Defines who can reach the host, database, media, logs, and backups; applies least privilege; reviews keys; and records access at the level its risk requires.
control_matrix.customer_or_provider: Customers choose workspace members and roles. Infrastructure providers control their own privileged-access programs.

control_matrix.application: Provides scoped deletion flows and durable media-cleanup jobs while protecting active publication, library, favorite, tag, template, and brand references.
control_matrix.managed_service: Makes the disclosed daily database and media recovery copies, prunes routine recovery history after 14 days, and performs the stated restore drill.
control_matrix.self_hosted_operator: Chooses backup location and retention, protects required secrets with the backup, tests restoration, and fulfills deletion obligations for its installation.
control_matrix.customer_or_provider: Customers resolve shared ownership and active billing blockers before account deletion and control provider-side content separately.

control_matrix.application: Pins supported toolchains and dependencies and includes formatting, lint, test, race, vulnerability, secret, workflow, browser, image, and restart-smoke gates in the release process.
control_matrix.managed_service: Deploys an immutable image only after the release workflow succeeds and verifies readiness and the exact running revision, with rollback when readiness fails.
control_matrix.self_hosted_operator: Tracks supported releases, evaluates security notices, updates the application and host, and verifies its own deployment and rollback path.
control_matrix.customer_or_provider: Dependency and infrastructure providers publish fixes for the components they maintain; customers report suspected vulnerabilities privately.

control_matrix.application: Emits service and authentication events, exposes readiness and version endpoints, and keeps provider responses and secrets out of normalized analytics and communication records.
control_matrix.managed_service: Uses size-bounded system and service journals and public readiness and revision checks. It does not claim a complete command-level operator audit trail.
control_matrix.self_hosted_operator: Chooses log access, retention, alerts, and monitoring and must avoid collecting secrets or more customer content than its operating need requires.
control_matrix.customer_or_provider: Infrastructure and social providers keep separate logs under their own controls; customers review their account and provider activity where available.

control_matrix.application: Provides a private security contact and keeps durable state needed to investigate failed jobs, authentication, and provider writes without intentionally storing reusable plaintext tokens in those records.
control_matrix.managed_service: Triages private reports, contains and repairs confirmed incidents, preserves only necessary evidence, notifies affected customers or authorities when required, and maintains the public incident wording on this page.
control_matrix.self_hosted_operator: Owns detection, containment, evidence, recovery, notifications, and post-incident work for its installation and coordinates with OpenPost when a product flaw is involved.
control_matrix.customer_or_provider: Report suspected OpenPost flaws privately, rotate exposed credentials, follow incident instructions, and contact the relevant provider when the event is provider-side.

control_matrix.control: Social networks, subprocessors, and user-requested services
control_matrix.application: Routes user-authorized provider actions through capability-specific adapters; automatic image captions use a generated thumbnail and bounded context.
control_matrix.managed_service: Publishes reviewed data-location, provider, transfer, and human-access facts and updates the register before a new service receives managed customer data.
control_matrix.self_hosted_operator: Chooses and configures its hosting, email, storage, AI, analytics, social apps, and optional services and publishes disclosures required for its users.
control_matrix.customer_or_provider: Customers choose social, identity, stock-media, and AI-triggering actions. Each selected provider controls its service, API, logs, and provider-side data.
